Class ModContext

java.lang.Object
com.happyuky7.openvoxelmoding.loader.ModContext
public final class ModContext extends Object
Services the OpenVoxel ModLoader offers to mods. One instance is shared by every mod and passed to each ClientMod hook.

Threads. Call these methods from the hooks (the game's main thread). From other threads, hand work back with ctx.engine().runOnMainThread(...).

Ids. Items use plain ids (iron_sword, stick), engine blocks use their names (stone, oak_log), and mod blocks use namespaced ids (mymod:ruby_block). Every method that takes an id accepts any of the three.

Dedicated servers. The same mod jar can run on a server through the ModLoader agent; there only ClientMod.onLoad(ModContext) runs, isServer() is true and client features are ignored.

    • registerCommand

      public void registerCommand(String name, String description, ModContext.CommandHandler handler)
      Registers a client chat command /name. It is listed by /chelp and completed with Tab. Client commands run before anything is sent to the server; unknown commands go to the server.
      Parameters:
      name - command name without the slash (case-insensitive)
      description - one line shown by /chelp, e.g. "<player> - greets someone"
      handler - called with the arguments

    • registerRecipe

      public boolean registerRecipe(String resultId, int resultCount, String[] pattern, String... keys)
      Adds a shaped crafting recipe. It matches at any position in the grid and mirrored; recipes up to 2x2 also work in the inventory grid, bigger ones need the crafting table. Safe to call in onLoad (it is applied once the game is ready). 
      ctx.registerRecipe("torch", 4, new String[]{"C", "S"}, "C", "coal", "S", "stick");
      Parameters:
      resultId - item id, block name or mod block id of the result
      resultCount - how many items one craft gives
      pattern - rows of the shape, one character per cell (space = empty)
      keys - pairs of character and ingredient id: "M", "iron_ingot", "S", "stick"
      Returns:
      false if an id is unknown or keys are not pairs (true when deferred during onLoad)

    • nativeBlock

      public NativeBlocks.Builder nativeBlock(String id)
      Starts the definition of a native block: a real engine block type, like block registration in Fabric or Forge. The game treats it like its own blocks (rendering, lighting, collision, mining, saving, networking, inventory). Call it from ClientMod.onLoad(ModContext) and finish with NativeBlocks.Builder.register(). 
      ctx.nativeBlock("mymod:ruby_block")
   .name("Ruby Block")
   .texture("assets/mymod/textures/ruby_block.png")
   .hardness(3f).tool("pickaxe", true)
   .register();
      For multiplayer, install the same mod jar on the server (ModLoader-Server/mods) and run the server with the ModLoader agent (ModLoader-Server/agent); both sides then agree on the ids.
      Parameters:
      id - namespaced id namespace:path, lowercase
      Returns:
      a builder; textures are read from the calling mod's jar
      See Also:
      • NativeBlocks

    • registerBlock

      public boolean registerBlock(String id, String displayName, String baseBlock, String topTexture, String sideTexture, String bottomTexture, ModContext.BlockUseHandler onUse)
      Registers a ModLoader block: a textured cube stored in the world as an engine block (baseBlock) plus a block code in its state. Prefer nativeBlock(String) for new blocks; this kind exists for blocks that need right-click behaviour or must work on servers without the agent.
      Parameters:
      id - namespaced id (mymod:ruby_block)
      displayName - name shown in the inventory when no translation exists
      baseBlock - engine block it is stored as (collision, mining, light), e.g. "STONE"
      topTexture - 16x16 PNG path inside your jar (required)
      sideTexture - side texture, or null for topTexture
      bottomTexture - bottom texture, or null for topTexture
      onUse - right-click handler, or null
      Returns:
      false if the id is invalid or taken, or a texture is missing
